title: Build a Virtual Trophy Room Your Club Can Search
description: Plan a virtual trophy room around checked winners, clear source records and simple search. Start with one trophy and share an online honours board.
html:
A virtual trophy room gives members an online way to explore a club's winners. It can show the history behind the cups in the cabinet, including records that are hard to find in old books or on engraved bases. Begin with the records you want people to find, then choose how to display them.

Decide what members should be able to find

Start with a few simple questions. Who won this cup in a given year? Which trophies did one person win? What events took place in a season? These questions help you decide what information to collect.

Trophy Guru's public honours board has views by year, trophy and person. Open the demo to try them. Its club and winner records are fictional examples, not a customer case study.

Build from sources your club can check

Gather photos of engraved cups, plates and boards. Include any old result sheets that help explain a gap. Take a full view of each trophy and clear close-ups of the names. Several angles can help when glare hides a letter.

AI can suggest names and years from these photos. A person must still check each reading. Do not treat a suggested name as proof. Keep unclear entries open until you can compare them with better sources.

Use the trophy photography guide to plan your first batch. The record review guide explains the next step.

Keep public and private records separate

Your working archive holds source photos, review notes and private member details. The public board presents the honours chosen for sharing. Preview the board and agree who can publish changes on behalf of the club.

Check names carefully before matching them to members. People with the same initials may be different winners. Keep enough evidence in the private archive for another volunteer to understand each decision.

Start with the website before buying a screen

Members can open the public board in a web browser. You can share its link without buying a dedicated touchscreen. If the club later wants a display in the clubhouse, test the board on the proposed screen first. Check text size, controls and the viewing distance.

The optional Intelligent Golf service has its own scope, price and availability. Read that page before planning an integration. The core archive and a paid website integration are separate choices.

Plan the work and the handover

Try one trophy from start to finish. Note the time spent taking photos, checking readings and fixing gaps. Use that result to estimate the next batch. The amount of review depends on the condition of your own records.

Export a CSV copy and pass on clear notes when the volunteer team changes. Keep the original trophies and source records. Add new winners each season, using the same checks as you used for historic names.

Use the club archive checklist to assign the work. Your first trophy is free, with up to 12 saved photos and no payment card. Try your own records before buying more credits.
